Answers, in match order first matching condition wins

#1 mood = miserable low-mood

Miserable, truth to tell. A day {activity} does not lift a mood like mine.

if asked “why?”

Because the day is long, and being {activity} takes more out of me than it gives back.

#2 mood = grumpy low-mood

Grumpy, if you must know. Ask me again when the day is done.

if asked “why?”

I have been {activity} all day, and it has worn my patience thin.

#3 mood = cheerful high-mood

Well enough to smile at you, Advisor. A day {activity} suits me today.

if asked “why?”

The work went kindly today and {settlement} has been good to me.

#4 mood = content high-mood

Content. Nothing broken, nothing missing that I can mend.

if asked “why?”

There is food in the house and the day has gone as it should.

#5 fallback

Calm. Steady as the week allows.

if asked “why?”

I keep to my work and my own business. That keeps a body calm.

  • do you enjoy your work
  • what did you do today
  • how was your day

Answers, in match order first matching condition wins

#1 role = guard duty

I keep the gate. {work} — watching who comes and goes, and mostly telling them to move along.

if asked “why?”

Somebody must stand there, and it is my turn.

#2 role = farmer labour

Farming. {work}, from before dawn until the light fails.

if asked “why?”

The soil does not wait for anyone's mood.

#3 role = artisan craft

I am a smith of my hands. {work} keeps me indoors and busy.

if asked “why?”

Good work cannot be hurried, and there is always more of it.

#4 role = trader trade

Trade. {work} — buying, selling, and remembering who owes what.

if asked “why?”

A market only feeds the people who are standing in it.

#5 role = labourer labour

Whatever needs carrying, I carry it. {work} today.

if asked “why?”

Strong arms are the only coin I was born with.

#6 time = night tired

Not now — the day's work is done and I want my bed.

if asked “why?”

The work starts again at first light whether I rest or not.

#7 fallback

Honest work, and plenty of it. {work} fills most days.

if asked “why?”

It keeps the roof on and the pot full.

  • what can you make

Answers, in match order first matching condition wins

#1 role = artisan craft

Metal, mostly. Give me a fire and an anvil and I will give you something that lasts.

if asked “why?”

A skill is the only thing nobody can tax away from you.

#2 role = farmer craft land

Reading weather and reading soil. Neither is written in any book.

if asked “why?”

The land teaches, and it charges for the lessons.

#3 fallback craft

I can mend more than I can make, and that has served well enough.

if asked “why?”

Practical hands are worth more here than clever ones.
